about: Chemical basis of drug action (CBDA) figures from Dr. Sikazwe's assigned Exam 1 pages; built by gen_cbda.py into cbda.js; checked by cbda_check.js.

species.name: Crisaborole as the tetrahedral boronate in the PDE4 site
species.teaching_note: Drawn after the slide 7 inset (J Med Chem 2021;64(24):17706-17727, as the slide cites): the boron bound to a third oxygen that bridges Zn2+ and Mg2+. The slide puts the negative charge on that oxygen; RDKit places the formal charge on the four-coordinate boron. Same atoms and bonds; not a PubChem compound record.

figures.title: Crisaborole: boron at the PDE4 zinc and magnesium
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 7 (its CBDA inset, from J Med Chem 2021;64(24):17706–17727, residues and dotted bonds as printed; the site outline is schematic). He: the boron group coordinates two cations, magnesium and zinc, in the PDE4 active site, “that is the basis” (11/03 T 712–719); intact drug binds the active site and stays there (T 786–793). The slide draws the negative charge on the bridging oxygen; RDKit puts it on the four-coordinate boron (same atoms and bonds).

figures.title: Methotrexate vs folic acid at DHFR
figures.caption: After DPAW slides 30–31 (structures, part colours and the slide 30 annotation “sits in the same enzyme cavity to competitively inhibit folic acid”); the cavity is schematic. He: methotrexate “goes in there and sits in the same enzyme cavity and competitively inhibits the binding of folic acid”, with the higher affinity (11/04 T@8900–@9230). The DHFR reduction itself: Reaction “Folate reduction by DHFR”.

figures.title: Cyclosporine: activated by cyclophilin
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 33 (“prodrug”; “Activated by complexation with cyclophilin receptor”; “Inhibits calcineurin phosphatase & T-cell signaling”; the slide’s ribbon diagram, PDB 1CWA, is shown here as labelled shapes). He: “how it’s bioactivated is not metabolic. It’s simply by its binding to its receptor”; the complex binds the active site (11/04 T@12378–@12620). Dr. Smith’s calcineurin–NFAT steps are in her figures.

figures.title: Tetracycline: chelation of metal ions
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 55 (ions as printed, including “Zn<sup>3+</sup>”; “insoluble salts”; food, dairy). The salt is drawn as a bracket because neither the slide nor the lecture names the binding atoms. He: the molecules chelate these elements, bone has a lot of calcium, the insoluble salts remain there and weaken bone or enamel (11/04 T@35844–@36050; “chelate” is transcribed “kill it”).

figures.title: Salicylate sunscreens: ester hydrolysis to salicylic acid
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 64 (“Salicylates (SA FG absorbs UVB & provides analgesia)”). The slide draws no reaction arrow; the hydrolysis is his spoken explanation: “They are esters, right, so they can undergo hydrolysis to give you salicylic acid” (11/04 T@42498–@42640). The alcohol released is not named on the slide, so it is not drawn.

figures.title: Hydroxy acids: alpha and beta
figures.caption: After DPAW slides 43–44 (slide 44 marks the α carbon and prints the SAR). He: “This is the alpha carbon. This one is called the beta carbon. So this is a beta hydroxy acid ... 2 carbon removed from the carboxylic acid” (11/04 T@22100–@22330). Polleve-4 (slide 45) is held and not drawn.

figures.title: Antiandrogens: biosynthesis vs receptor
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 53 (steroidal and non-steroidal antiandrogens, with Louis’s notes “diminish testosterone biosynthesis” and “prevent testosterone from binding to its receptor”). He: spironolactone and ketoconazole decrease testosterone biosynthesis; azole antifungals are strong 3A4 inhibitors; flutamide blocks testosterone from binding its receptor (11/04 T@32237–@33000).

figures.title: Retinoids: C13 isomers; exposed acid vs ester
figures.caption: After DPAW slides 49 (“All-trans retinoic acid”; “13-cis retinoic acid”; “Geometric isomer of Tretinoin”) and 51 (3rd generation, poly-aromatic; tazarotene “a prodrug”). Ringed: the C13 double bond, counted from the COOH end as he counted it, trans in tretinoin and cis in isotretinoin (11/04 T@28100–@28700). Shaded: the exposed carboxylic acid that makes adapalene and trifarotene directly active, and tazarotene’s ethyl ester (11/04 T@29800–@30300); its hydrolysis is the Reaction “Tazarotene to tazarotenic acid”.

figures.title: Pimecrolimus vs tacrolimus: two differences, one lactone
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 28 (structures; Cl and the ethyl of pimecrolimus, OH and the allyl of tacrolimus highlighted; cLogP 6.0 and 5.8; skin protein binding) and slide 32 (Polleve-3: lactone = cyclic ester). He: “The only points of difference are that chlorine and that methyl group, and here you have that [allyl] group and hydroxy”; pimecrolimus binds to the skin, tacrolimus has low skin binding and can go in (11/04 T@4400–@5600). Both act as calcineurin inhibitors (slide 28).

figures.title: Hydrocortisone to clobetasol propionate
figures.caption: After DPAW slide 25 (the dashed arrow and the changes it highlights; potency rests on structure, delivery vehicle and concentration) and slide 20 (SAR). Slide 25 draws clobetasol propionate with OH on C21; the marketed drug’s 21-Cl is drawn here, as in the Atlas (reviews/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md notes the slide’s drawing error). He: these derivative structures need not be memorized; structural changes, not metabolism, raise the potency (11/03 T 1152–1154, 1175–1179).
